**Persistent cloud cover, frequent showers, and the active southwest monsoon (habagat) are the main factors capping Manila’s daytime maximum on August 14, 2026.**  

These conditions sharply reduce solar heating compared with clearer-sky climatology, where August highs average near 31 °C. Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble models show a broad 25–33 °C envelope with 90–100 % rain probability and overcast skies, while real-time observations confirm thick cloud decks and scattered thunderstorms that limit insolation and promote evaporative cooling. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probability (70.9 %) to a 27 °C peak, with rapidly declining odds above 28 °C, reflecting the expectation that monsoon-driven moisture and reduced sunshine will keep the daily maximum well below seasonal norms. New model runs or breaks in the cloud cover remain the key near-term variables that could shift resolution.

Long-term averages show typical highs of 23–26 °C (roughly 73–79 °F), driven by cooler, drier air masses from the south and limited solar heating under partly cloudy or hazy skies. No major synoptic features—such as an approaching cold front, warm advection, or clear-sky radiative heating—are indicated that would push temperatures outside the 23–27 °C envelope. Recent days have produced actual maxima around 24–28 °C, reinforcing trader expectations that the day’s peak will most probably settle between 24 °C and 26 °C. The market’s probability distribution therefore reflects both the narrow historical variability of August afternoons in the city and the absence of any short-term meteorological catalyst capable of shifting the outcome materially higher or lower.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pa/panama-city/MPMG.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts for Panama City show afternoon thunderstorms and extensive cloud cover likely moderating peak temperatures on August 15 amid the active rainy season. High atmospheric moisture and the positioning of the Intertropical Convergence Zone promote convective activity that reduces solar insolation and releases latent heat aloft, typically capping daytime maxima near 30–32°C. Model guidance from regional sources indicates scattered showers with highs around 31°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies, though variability in storm timing and intensity creates uncertainty between the closely matched market leaders at 30–32°C. Historical August averages near 30–32°C provide context, with no anomalous heat ridge or clear-sky conditions evident to push readings higher.
